todaysEvents.summary: Hormuz traffic falls to nine vessels
todaysEvents.delta: Reuters reported Sep 25 from Kpler data that commodity-vessel transits fell to nine on Sep 24 from 14; the 10-day average was 18. Crude exports were 33.7 million barrels week-to-date, with 19 tankers including 17 VLCCs.

todaysEvents.summary: Saudi crude exports rebound through Hormuz
todaysEvents.delta: Reuters said Saudi crude exports via Hormuz are on track for 3.6 million bpd in September, up from about 0.9 million bpd in August. Gulf of Oman ship-to-ship transfer capacity has reached its limit, raising tanker and delay pressure.

Reuters reported Brent at $105.11 and WTI at $92.61 at 0541 GMT as negotiators explored a phased deal. Saudi Arabia said it intercepted six Houthi missiles aimed at Taif and the Yanbu area; no signed Hormuz reopening is verified.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Indirect talks produce a signed, monitored reopening and verified shipping normalisation. Saudi East-West pumping is building, but Reuters says Yanbu tanker loadings have yet to resume; QatarEnergy force majeure remains reported through November.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: Talks continue without an agreed reopening; Sep 24 commodity-vessel transits fall to nine, Saudi exports require heavy Hormuz tanker and ship-to-ship activity, and Qatar replacement LNG remains constrained.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Conditional talks fail or Houthi and Iran-linked attacks widen, keeping Hormuz traffic selective and Gulf ship-to-ship operations congested; Qatar output and route costs remain unverified.
